rows.title: Key lemma: integrate the first-event density
rows.text: For any continuous real function l, put L(s)=∫₀ˢl(u)du. The fundamental theorem gives L′=l. The chain rule yields (1−exp(−L))′=l exp(−L). The derivative is continuous, so integrating from0 to t≥0 gives the endpoint difference; L(0)=0 removes the lower endpoint. Nonnegativity is not needed for this identity; the actual nonnegative rate will supply it for the measure.

rows.title: Key lemma: turn the integral into finite density mass
rows.text: Now assume l(s)≥0 for every real s. The exponential is positive and the density continuous, hence integrable on every bounded (0,t]. The integral of ofReal(density) equals ofReal of its real integral. Evaluating withDensity on the whole line and using the preceding identity gives the exact ENNReal mass, including t=0.

rows.title: Key lemma: determine the density CDF on a finite window
rows.text: For a≥0 and t≥0, intersect the window (0,t] with (−∞,a]. This is (0,min(t,a)]. Restriction composition and the previous mass formula give the left-half-line mass. This step uses only measurable interval identities and preserves the finite-window cutoff.

rows.title: Key lemma: compute the positive finite clock mass
rows.text: For a measurable extended nonnegative wait U under a probability measure, assume the already derived survival P(U>t)=exp(−L(t)) and L(0)=0. Then P(U>0)=1. The event 0<U≤t is {U>0} minus its measurable subset {U>t}; finite-measure subtraction gives mass1−exp(−L(t)). This includes infinite waits correctly in the subtracted tail.

rows.title: Key lemma: the projected clock has the same CDF
rows.text: On 0<U≤t the wait is finite. For a≥0, the preimage of (−∞,a] under untopD0 intersected with that event equals {0<U≤min(t,toNNReal(a))}. The proof splits U=∞ and finite U explicitly; the infinite case cannot satisfy either finite cutoff. Pushforward evaluation, restriction and the preceding mass formula give the CDF. The zero default outside the restricted event never creates an atom.

rows.title: Retain the actual definitions and consume their compiled producers
rows.text: Use the literal actual clocks, flow, zero-normal-safe reflection, nonnegative rate, stopped hazard clock, positive finite event, density and mark. Consume the actual hazard/flow/bounce producers with exactly the six original analytic assumptions. UnitExponentialProduct supplies P probability. These are internal proof dependencies, not premises supplied by the theorem caller.

rows.title: Derive actual rate continuity, clock law and Borel mark
rows.text: The compiled jointly continuous harmonic flow and bounce-rate continuity give the continuous free-arc rate l(s)≥0 for all real s. The jointly measurable stopped clock composed with real threshold truncation and coordinate0 gives U; untopD0 and inclusion give F. The compiled Borel reflection composed with the flow gives J. Map composition identifies U under P with the Exp(1) stopped-clock law, hence P(U>t)=exp(−Λ(t)). Joint continuity of Λ and truncation also give continuous nonnegative d.

rows.title: Identify the actual finite density and its entire measure
rows.text: Fix T. A_T is the intersection of two Borel clock events. On (0,T], toNNReal(s) has real value s, so the literal d agrees almost everywhere on this support with l(s)exp(−∫₀ˢl). For a≥0, the two CDF lemmas agree after converting min(T,toNNReal(a)) to min(T,a). For a<0, F is nonnegative and (0,T] has empty intersection with (−∞,a], so both masses vanish. The left pushforward is finite; equality on every left half-line therefore identifies the whole measures.

rows.title: Map the same finite law through the actual post-bounce mark
rows.text: The equality with the restricted-clock pushforward proves ρ finite. Borel J and measurable map composition then give the marked law using the very same J, F and restricted P. Evaluating the density on the whole line gives1−exp(−Λ(T)); Λ(T)≥0 makes this a nonnegative number and positivity of exp makes it at most1. No division by that mass occurs.

rows.title: Derive all three integrability statements
rows.text: For any displayed Borel h with |h|≤M, finiteness of the marked measure gives h∈L¹; the measurable composed clock test is bounded under the finite restriction of P and is also L¹. The same bound gives h∘J∈L¹(ρ). The withDensity integrability equivalence transfers this last fact to (ofReal(d)).toReal·h∘J under restricted Lebesgue measure. Since d≥0 and ofReal(d)<∞, that function is exactly h(J(s))d(s). Thus weighted integrability is derived, including M=0.

rows.title: Transfer the bounded-test integral exactly
rows.text: Rewrite the marked law as the measurable pushforward of restricted P and apply the Bochner integral-map identity. Apply integral-map once more through J to integrate h∘J under ρ. Finally the withDensity integral identity and nonnegative d replace the ENNReal weight by its real value. This yields the stated weighted finite-event integral. Successive conditional factors and the final-survival/path expansion require additional proofs.
